question: Which Mauryan ruler was called Amitrochates by the Greeks?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bindusara.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mauryan ruler **who was called **Amitrochates** by the Greeks was** Bindusara.**
 
• Amitrochates means** "Slayer of Enemies" **in Greek, which shows the **military prowess** of Bindusara.
 
• Bindusara was the son of **Chandragupta Maurya**, who founded the Mauryan Empire in **321 BCE.**
 
• Bindusara expanded the Mauryan Empire by **conquering the Deccan region** and parts of South India.
 
• He was succeeded by his son, the famous **Emperor Ashoka,** who is known for his conversion to **Buddhism and promotion of non-violence.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Samudragupta **was a Gupta Emperor who ruled from **335-375 CE **and was known for his military conquests and patronage of the arts.
 
• **Kanishka** was a Kushan Emperor who ruled from **127-151 CE** and was known for his patronage of Buddhism and the arts.
 
• **Chandragupta I **was a Gupta Emperor who ruled from **320-335 CE** and was known for his military conquests and patronage of the arts.
